name: Cornerlessness Can Be pc-Minimal without Forbiddenness
statement: Let $S$ be an ample forbidden pc-minor whose only corner is a root $0$, and let $P$ be a nontrivial corner-peelable ample family whose only corner is $0$. Assume every proper root-preserving pc-minor of either family peels to its root. On disjoint irredundant coordinate sets, the wedge $X=S\vee P$ is ample and cornerless, every nonempty proper pc-minor of $X$ has a corner, and every nonpeelable pc-minor contains $S$. Thus $S$ is the unique forbidden pc-minor of $X$ up to isomorphism, and $X$ has no cornerless forbidden pc-minor.
proof: Vertex gluing preserves ampleness. Nonroot vertices retain the multiple maximal cubes of their own piece, while neighbours of the root in the two blocks have no mixed completing square, so the root is not a corner. Every minor either lies in one block or retains the root and splits as $S\'\vee P\'$. If $S\'$ is proper, peel it to the root and then peel $P\'$. A nonpeelable minor therefore retains $S$; when it is proper, $P\'$ is proper and supplies a corner, including the root when $P\'=\{0\}$. Forbidden minimality then makes $S$ the unique forbidden minor.
